# Problem 5: A degrade path for the scene

## MEASURED A/B (2026-09-01, runtime-patched live page, SwiftShader; gains in ms per frame vs same-load baseline; 4x = CPU-throttled weak-machine proxy; control drift 0.4ms at 1x, 0.04ms at 4x)

**The preset as first specced measured NO gain at the dock view (-3.3 at 4x, i.e. inside/below noise)** - its levers (bloom pyramid 0.125, reflection buffer 0.125, second sheet off, trail 5) all act on parts that were already cheap there; the dock cost is water fragments + the full-res composite, which the preset never touched. REVISED recommendation: the weak-machine preset should be built from what measured - the ripple gate (+4.9), trail 5 (kills burst spikes), cheap-bleed (+1.25), single sheet (+0.5) - with the buffer shrinks dropped. The whole recommended stack measured **+5.6ms at 4x with the typical dock frame back at 16.7ms (60fps)**. Option C (reduced-motion) is unaffected: it was never a perf claim.

---


**Status quo (MEASURED, verified in code):** the scene ships identical work to every machine. There is no capability probe and no reduced-motion path in any scene file (`_javascript/three-shared.js`, `three-background-scene.js`, `three-background-minimal.js`, `shader/kawaseBloom.js`, `shader/mirroredSurface.js`, `lantern-controller.js`, `firework-controller.js` all read only `CONFIG`). The only reduced-motion gate near the scene is the fireworks greeting (`_javascript/modules/components/fireworks-toggle.js:22,34-36`). Measured reality: 30.8ms avg at the About dock view under SwiftShader, 99.9ms single frames on the throttled portal, 4.2ms on an RTX 3080.

A note on coverage: the "minimal" tier pages (portal, projects, ramblings) load the SAME full-scene bundle with dock and water hidden (`assets/js/effects/scene-mode.js:17-27`, `_includes/chrome-scripts.html:45-47`), so every knob below in the scene entry file also covers them. The 404's embers bundle only goes through `createBaseScene`, so it gets the bloom and paper knobs and nothing else, which is all it has.

## Option A: boot-time detection, reduced preset for software rasterisers

Read the GPU name once at renderer creation; if it is a software rasteriser, halve the two render-target scales, halve the firework trail, and drop the second paper sheet. Machines with a real GPU see byte-identical output. Unrecognised strings change nothing (fail-safe to today's behavior).

### Code

**`_javascript/three-shared.js`** , insert after line 42 (`renderer.setSize(...)`), before the composer block:

```js
  /* Boot probe: a software rasteriser (hardware accel off) runs this scene at 30fps where a real
     GPU idles at 4ms, so it gets a reduced preset. An unrecognised string changes nothing. */
  const gl = renderer.getContext();
  const dbg = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info');
  const gpuName = String(gl.getParameter(dbg ? dbg.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL : gl.RENDERER));
  const softwareGPU = /SwiftShader|llvmpipe|softpipe|Software/i.test(gpuName);
```

**`_javascript/three-shared.js:57`** , bloom buffer scale:

```js
// before
    scale: CONFIG.lanterns.bloom.scale,
// after
    scale: softwareGPU ? CONFIG.lanterns.bloom.scale / 2 : CONFIG.lanterns.bloom.scale,
```

**`_javascript/three-shared.js:72`** , second paper sheet. `kawaseBloom.js:353-354` already zeroes the mix when slot 1 is empty, so one gate skips both the per-pixel fetch and the texture download:

```js
// before
  bloomPass.setPaperTexture(paperLoader.load(`/assets/tex/${paper.sheet2}.png`), 1);
// after
  if (!softwareGPU) bloomPass.setPaperTexture(paperLoader.load(`/assets/tex/${paper.sheet2}.png`), 1);
```

**`_javascript/three-shared.js:99`** , hand the flag to the entry files:

```js
// before
  return { scene, camera, renderer, composer, bloomPass };
// after
  return { scene, camera, renderer, composer, bloomPass, softwareGPU };
```

**`_javascript/three-background-scene.js:24`**:

```js
// before
const { scene, camera, renderer, composer, bloomPass } = createBaseScene();
// after
const { scene, camera, renderer, composer, bloomPass, softwareGPU } = createBaseScene();
```

**`_javascript/three-background-scene.js:28`** , firework trail (400 particles x 10 ghost copies per shell, `firework-controller.js:52-55`). Written into `CONFIG` so the degraded value is visible in `window.THREEJS_CONFIG` and the scene tuner, no hidden state:

```js
// before
const fireworkController = new FireworkController(scene, camera, CONFIG.fireworks);
// after
if (softwareGPU) CONFIG.fireworks.particleTrail = 5;   // 400 particles x 10 ghosts is the fill cost
const fireworkController = new FireworkController(scene, camera, CONFIG.fireworks);
```

**`_javascript/three-background-scene.js:48`** , reflection target (the second full-scene render, `mirroredSurface.js:42-60`):

```js
// before
  mirroredSurface = new MirroredSurface(scene, camera, renderer, waterMesh, {
    reflectionIntensity: CONFIG.water.reflection.reflectionIntensity,
// after
  mirroredSurface = new MirroredSurface(scene, camera, renderer, waterMesh, {
    reflectionScale: softwareGPU ? 0.125 : 0.25,   // 0.25 = the default at mirroredSurface.js:51
    reflectionIntensity: CONFIG.water.reflection.reflectionIntensity,
```

### Predicted saving (About bottom, SwiftShader, against the measured 30.8ms avg)

| Knob | Basis | Predicted |
|---|---|---|
| Bloom scale 0.25 to 0.125 | bloom off = -3.2 MEASURED; halving the scale quarters the four blur-chain renders, the full-size composite stays | -1.5 to -2.5ms INFERENCE |
| Reflection 0.25 to 0.125 | reflection off = -5.8 MEASURED at top; quarter the fragments, scene render submitted at the same 104-118 draw calls | -2 to -4ms INFERENCE |
| Second sheet off | paper off entirely = -4.4 MEASURED; this removes one of up to 3 extra fetches | -0.5 to -1ms INFERENCE |
| Trail 10 to 5 | 8 shells p95 33.4 MEASURED; halves per-shell vertex and fill work | burst spikes roughly halved, portal 99.9 spikes included, INFERENCE |

Total at the dock view: roughly -4 to -7.5ms of the 12.5ms over the vsync floor, so ~30fps becomes ~38-45fps. **Honest limit: A alone does not restore 60fps there.** The residual is the water surface shader itself (water hidden = -4.1 MEASURED, 8 snoise calls + the 16-slot ripple loop, `mirroredSurface.js:138-201`) and the base render, which are separate problems. If the re-measure wants more, the one escalation knob that touches every pass is the pixel ratio (`three-shared.js:41`, gate `0.5` down to `0.35` under `softwareGPU`), but 0.5 is a Rod-judged number paired with the paper look, so that is its own taste call, not part of this preset.

**Visual risk: subtle, and only on machines currently running at 30fps.** Chunkier bloom halo and a blurrier reflection (both are exactly what the paper filter was judged to mask, `three-config.js:31-34`), the fine coldpress grain inside the washi structure disappears (washi stays), firework trails thinner. Real-GPU machines: zero change. Caveat (INFERENCE): Firefox with fingerprinting resistance masks the GPU string, so those users keep full quality even when software-rendered; the failure direction is "no worse than today".

**Line delta:** about +9. Against D5: this is the minimum code any degrade path can be, one probe, four knobs at their existing call sites, no state, no cache, no new abstraction.

**Prefer when:** you want the measured problem (software rasterisers) fixed with the least code and no behavior change anywhere else.

## Option B: measured auto-degrade (the frame timer decides)

Sample real frame deltas after load; if the median is over budget, pull levers one at a time until it is not. Catches slow machines the string probe cannot name (old iGPUs at large viewports). This is the most code.

### Code

**`_javascript/three-shared.js`** , new export (about 20 lines):

```js
/* Measured degrade: if the median frame is still over budget after load, pull the next lever and
   re-measure. One-way, quality never steps back up (stepping up re-creates the jank it fixed).
   First step needs real jank (p50 > 25ms); further steps chase the 17ms vsync floor. */
export function autoDegrade(steps) {
  const deltas = [];
  let last = 0;
  let threshold = 25;
  function tick(now) {
    if (last && now - last < 250) deltas.push(now - last);   // skip tab-switch gaps
    last = now;
    if (deltas.length >= 120) {
      const p50 = deltas.sort((a, b) => a - b)[60];
      if (p50 <= threshold || !steps.length) return;         // healthy or out of levers: stop forever
      steps.shift()();
      threshold = 17;
      deltas.length = 0;
    }
    requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  }
  addEventListener('load', () => requestAnimationFrame(tick));
}
```

**`_javascript/three-background-scene.js`** , after the animation loop starts (import `autoDegrade` from three-shared):

```js
autoDegrade([
  () => { if (mirroredSurface) { mirroredSurface.reflectionScale = 0.125; mirroredSurface.handleResize(); } },
  () => { bloomPass.scale = 0.125; bloomPass.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight); },
  () => { fireworkController.config.particleTrail = 5; },      // future shells only
  () => { bloomPass.setPaperTexture(null, 1); },               // drops the second paper sheet
]);
```

(All four levers verified against existing setters: `handleResize` re-derives the target from `reflectionScale` at `mirroredSurface.js:335-339`, `setSize` re-derives the bloom chain from `this.scale` at `kawaseBloom.js:286-298`, the trail is read per shell at `firework-controller.js:272`, the empty slot-1 texture zeroes the mix at `kawaseBloom.js:354`.)

**`_javascript/three-background-minimal.js`** , same idea, two-lever ladder (bloom, sheet), about 4 lines.

**Predicted saving:** same ceiling as A on SwiftShader (it converges on the same preset, a few seconds later). Its only extra win is unknown slow real-GPU machines, a class we have not measured.

**Visual risk: visible.** The degrade happens while the visitor watches, the reflection pops blurrier mid-session. Worse, rAF deltas measure the whole main thread, so image decode, layout, or scroll jank during load can degrade a perfectly healthy machine (INFERENCE, this is the standard failure mode of frame-time governors). And the measured portal problem, 99.9ms single frames during bursts, lives in the p95, which a p50 trigger never sees.

**Line delta:** about +30. **D5 verdict: fails.** A window buffer, a threshold state, per-page lever lists, and a controller loop, all to cover a machine class we have no measurement of, while the measured class (SwiftShader) is already caught by A's four-line probe. Not worth it until a real device shows up that A misses.

**Prefer when:** a report arrives of a slow machine whose GPU string looks normal. Keep this diff in the drawer for that day.

## Option C: the scene's reduced-motion path (D21 debt, independent of perf)

Not a perf option, zero frame saving by design, no change for anyone who has not set the OS preference. This is the missing accessibility path: the scene stays as a lit, still picture; only motion the visitor did not ask for stops. User-driven motion stays (scroll camera, click fireworks, mouse avoidance), matching WCAG intent that self-initiated interaction is fine.

What stops and what stays:

| Subsystem | Verdict | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Paper boil (3.25Hz re-roll, the one flagged near the 2.3.1 frequency line) | STOPS | `boilHz: 0` takes the existing static branch, `kawaseBloom.js:361-369` |
| Lantern float + ember flutter | STOPS | both multiply `CONFIG.lanterns.float.amount`, `lantern-controller.js:173-175` |
| Water wave motion (`uTime`) | STOPS | freeze the time advance; the reflection still tracks the scroll camera |
| Auto greeting | already gated | `fireworks-toggle.js:34-36`, nothing to do |
| Click ripples | STOPS (forced) | with `uTime` frozen a ripple never ages and paints a permanent ring at the click point (`mirroredSurface.js:189-199`), so the spawn is gated too |
| Static lit scene, bloom, paper texture, scroll camera, click fireworks, mouse avoidance | STAYS | untouched |
| Lantern flicker (brightness shimmer, `lanternShader.js:94-98`) | Rod's call | arguably "blinking" under 2.2.2; stopping it fully needs the ember literals gated too (`three-background-scene.js:96-98`, `three-background-minimal.js:55-57`), +2 lines. Left ON in this diff. |

### Code

**`_javascript/three-shared.js`** , after `export { CONFIG };` (line 10):

```js
/* The scene's reduced-motion path (D21). The scene stays lit and still; only motion the visitor
   did not ask for stops. Boot-time read, same as every other module on the site. */
export const STILL = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
if (STILL) CONFIG.lanterns.float.amount = 0;   // lantern float and ember flutter share this knob
```

**`_javascript/three-shared.js:66`**:

```js
// before
    paperBoilHz: paper.boilHz
// after
    paperBoilHz: STILL ? 0 : paper.boilHz   // 0 takes the existing static branch
```

**`_javascript/three-background-scene.js:126`** (add `STILL` to the line 11-20 import):

```js
// before
  { update: () => { if (mirroredSurface) mirroredSurface.update(); } },
// after
  // STILL freezes uTime; the reflection still tracks the scroll camera, which is user motion.
  { update: () => { if (mirroredSurface) mirroredSurface.update(STILL ? 0 : 1); } },
```

**`_javascript/three-background-scene.js:71-72`** , ripple guard:

```js
// before
  addEventListener('pointerup', (e) => {
    if (!mirroredSurface) return;
// after
  addEventListener('pointerup', (e) => {
    /* frozen uTime would pin a spawned ripple at age 0 forever: permanent ring at the click */
    if (!mirroredSurface || STILL) return;
```

**Visual risk:** none for anyone without the preference set. With it set: a still nightscape (the deliberate outcome).

**Line delta:** about +6. Against D5: it is the one-matchMedia-check version the debt note asked for, every stop rides an existing zero branch or existing knob, no new mechanism.

**Prefer when:** always; it is not competing with A or B, it is the independent D21 debt riding the same knobs.

## Rod looks once (all on a weak machine: Chrome with hardware acceleration off, or `--disable-gpu`)

1. **About dock view (bottom of scroll)** with A applied: reflection blurrier, bloom halo chunkier, coldpress inner grain gone from the paper. The question is whether the paper still sells it as print.
2. **One firework volley** (click a few, let the greeting run) with A applied: trails at 5 ghosts instead of 10.
3. **With OS reduced-motion switched on** (any machine): the still nightscape, and a judgment on whether the lantern flicker shimmer should also stop (the +2 line variant in C's table).

## Recommendation

Ship **A + C** (about +15 lines total): A's four-line probe exactly matches the machine class the measurements were taken on and fails safe everywhere else, C clears the D21 debt through the same knobs for near-zero code. Hold B until a slow machine appears that A's string probe cannot name; its diff is written above when that happens.
